Everton look like the far likelier side to break the deadlock. De Zerbi’s changes have done little to affect the game. Marmoush is cutting a very frustrated figure up top for Spurs.

Bergvall finds Savio with a whipped cross. The winger tries to help the ball back into the danger zone, but Pickford reacts quickly and collects possession.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

What is Kinsky doing?! The goalkeeper’s dreadful pass which was intended for Tonali is intercepted by Dewsbury-Hall, who tries to slide a low effort through Kinsky’s legs. The Tottenham man redeems himself with a crucial save to keep the scoreline goalless. The hosts are living so dangerously. Kinsky needs to wake up.

Antonín Kinský redeems himself after Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall fails to take advantage! 😮 pic.twitter.com/nuKZju90Wz

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

Enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

The start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. That day, Tottenham allowed Newcastle to seize the initiative and they netted two second-half goals without reply. Everton are gaining confidence as Spurs continue to lack courage or threat. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Tottenham fail to clear a corner and the ball lands at George’s feet. The Everton winger shoots but his fierce drive is blocked by Bentancur. The whole of Spurs’ bench is warming up. The visitors currently have the momentum and the hosts look nervous.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

George does brilliantly to escape away from Gray and floats a cross towards the back post. Barry rises highest and his close-range header is blocked by Kinsky. The Tottenham goalkeeper didn’t know much about it, but that’s a massive stop. Undoubtedly the game’s most dangerous moment in front of goal so far.

Spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

Ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

We are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

An uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

There will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

There has not been a single attempt on target at 40:27 from either team. Spurs have had the best of it but even so. That’s a poor return.

Another attack fizzles out for Spurs. Substitute Jack Grealish engaging in some badinage with home fans as he warms up. He famously agreed a move to Spurs in 2018, called off at the eleventh hour when Aston Villa were sold to the current ownership.

That is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

Pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

Tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

Tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

Maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

There is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

Gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Garner’s corner is cleared by Spurs, but only as far as Maitland-Niles. In similar range to where he scored that stunning equaliser against Manchester United, the former Arsenal man shoots, but his attempt fizzes well wide.

Spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Big question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

Sávio has had a fine start to the game. Mykolenko in for a long afternoon. Spurs have looked dangerous and should be 1-0 up.

Tonali finds Savio with a deep cross, leaving Pickford in no-man’s land. The Brazilian keeps the ball in play and it loops up, just out of Marmoush’s reach.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

Spurs then burst forward again through Savio, who feeds Fernandes. The playmaker’s low drive is heroically blocked by Tarkowski as Everton continue to hold on (just about).

As expected, it’s Tottenham with all the early possession, with Everton sitting very deep and soaking up the early pressure. Marmoush turns Armstrong and wins a free-kick in a dangerous area.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

Greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. The mood will sour further if Spurs do not win today. No Porro or Udogie so Archie Gray, ever adaptable, starts at right-back again.

Everton are undefeated with five points from three games. They have a decent 16/17 players but it is the reserves beyond that which everyone is concerned about. Grealish and Dibling on the bench give them two potential game-changers. Spurs’ squad looks very strong on the team-sheet. A full bench of experienced pros and no fillers. On the pitch it has been less convincing.

"Solanke is a crucial player"Roberto De Zerbi on the importance of Dominic Solanke being fit for Spurs 💪 pic.twitter.com/FNWNsTWdt8

Coventry City vs Brighton & Hove Albion (14:00)

Manchester United vs Manchester City (16:30)

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

The Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

“We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” says Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

🎧🫡 Thierno Barry ahead of today's clash in North London. pic.twitter.com/mwlsKH8Pid

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van de Ven, Van Hecke, Robertson; Tonali, Bentancur, Fernandes; Savio, Solankem, Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Tel, Bergvall, Kudus, Davies.

Everton: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Brathwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.

Subs: Travers, O’Brien, Keane, King, Alcaraz, Graham, Hackney, Dibling, Grealish.

After scoring that last-minute leveller against Manchester United last time out, Ainsley Maitland-Niles is promoted to the starting 11 and replaces Merlin Rohl. Brennan Johnson returns to his former club and starts, while Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @SpursOfficial. COYB! ✊#TOTEVE pic.twitter.com/mOcCayRUfm

Roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1508. Bayern Munich stance on signing Real Madrid's Trent Alexander-Arnold 'revealed'

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:32

Bayern Munich are reportedly not interested in signing Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold in the near future.

Alexander-Arnold established himself as arguably one of the finest right-backs in Premier League history during his time at Liverpool, but he has struggled to reproduce that form since joining Real Madrid.

The England international has gradually slipped down the pecking order at the Santiago Bernabeu under Jose Mourinho, with Federico Valverde and Denzel Dumfries seemingly ahead of him.

Alexander-Arnold was also subjected to boos from sections of the home support following his lacklustre performance in Real Madrid's 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo last week.

Former Liverpool and England striker Emile Heskey recently suggested that Alexander-Arnold should consider a move to Bayern, although he admitted he would love to see the defender return to Anfield.

However, Bild journalist Christian Falk has categorically dismissed the links, suggesting that Bayern are more interested in signing players such as Givairo Read than Alexander-Arnold.

Bayern already have Konrad Laimer and Josip Stanisic available for the right-back position, while Sacha Boey also remains at the club.

Even if Vincent Kompany decides to make changes in that department, he would reportedly favour a younger profile, meaning Alexander-Arnold is unlikely to be a genuine option for the German champions.

Speaking to CFBayern Insider, Falk said: "It is not true - Bayern Munich are interested in Real Madrid fullback Trent Alexander-Arnold. Bayern are searching for a player in this position, and players like Givairo Read are definitely still of interest.

"You can tell from Read’s profile alone that the club just isn’t looking to add a player like Alexander-Arnold to the ranks. Also, I’m not sure if Vincent Kompany would look at the Englishman’s profile, as he’s not a typical right-back for Bayern Munich.

"He’s also not the youngest footballer any more. And, if we’re being honest, the 28-year-old hasn’t proven himself at Real Madrid.

"You have to have a lot of respect for English players who give it a go playing in another country. But not every English player succeeds after leaving the UK, and not every English player is Harry Kane! So, I don’t think Alexander-Arnold will be a genuine option for Bayern in the summer."

While an emotional return to Anfield would appeal to many supporters, the reality is that Liverpool have probably moved on, even though the right-back position remains a somewhat problematic area for them.

Jeremie Frimpong has yet to convince everyone, while there is also uncertainty over whether the Reds will sign Ronald Araujo from Barcelona on a permanent deal.

With Conor Bradley's injury record remaining a concern and Joe Gomez potentially departing next summer, Andoni Iraola could look to bring in a new right-back, although it remains doubtful whether Liverpool would consider a move for their former player.

#1507. Plenty of praise rightly distributed: Player ratings for Milan-Frosinone from Italian papers

Several AC Milan players have been highly praised by the Italian media after the 5-1 dismantling of Frosinone at San Siro.

Milan ended up with goals from five different sources as Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted, in addition to the opening goal which was an own-goal by Calvani. Adrien Rabiot got three assists, while Diego Moreira shone too.

It was a statement result and a ruthless display of the weapons that the Rossoneri have in transition, and it moves Ruben Amorim’s side back into the top four, while they remain five points off leaders Lazio.

Starting with La Gazzetta dello Sport, they gave the team’s overall performance a score of 8 out of 10, which is the same mark that they gave Amorim for his selections and tactical handling of what could have been a tough game on paper.

Rabiot was the Serie A Man of the Match and he gets the crown from La Gazzetta too, scoring an 8. The worst performer was Davide Bartesaghi, who struggled in his battle with Ghedjemis and got a 5.5.

Moreira matched Rabiot with an 8, while Pulisic and Luka Modric were given a 7.5. Four players scored a 7: Yunus Musah, Ramos, Jashari and Cisse. Sankhoun Diawara (6.5) passed the test, with Koni De Winter, Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan being given a 6.

Corriere dello Sport were a tad harsher with their scoring, giving Rabiot a 7.5 as the highest score. Jashari, Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and Ramos were handed a 7. They gave Cisse a 6.5, and everyone else got a passing score. Amorim (7.5) was also praised.

Tuttosport meanwhile gave Rabiot an 8, distributing 7.5s instead to Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and the coach Amorim. Scores of 7 went to Jashari, Musah, Ramos and Cisse. Gila, De Winter and Diawara got given a 6.5, and everyone else a 6.

#1504. Report: Liverpool transfer blow could lead to surprise January deal

Liverpool's recruitment drive looks set to continue this winter.

The Reds have spent over £650 million since winning the Premier League in 2025, but the rebuild is far from complete.

Julian Ward has taken the reigns within the Anfield recruitment team and work is now being done to action some of the club's winter plans.

Andoni Iraola's side aren't the only team looking to do business in January though, and a European giant could spoil the plans of the Merseyside club.

The potential transfer blow would frustrate Liverpool but could open the door for another deal to be completed sooner than planned.

Barcelona join race for Liverpool targetThe Reds are in the market for defensive reinforcements, and VfB Stuttgart standout Finn Jeltsch has been one of the most exciting names linked with a Merseyside move. The Reds are in the market for defensive reinforcements, and VfB Stuttgart standout Finn Jeltsch has been one of the most exciting names linked with a Merseyside move.

Liverpool are one of many top European clubs monitoring the 20-year-old German defender, who has played in every Bundesliga game for Stuttgart so far this season.

Ward will hope that he can be the man to win the race for Jeltsch, but if Liverpool don't sign the 20-year-old then a move to Barcelona could be a boost for the Reds too.

#1503. Liverpool transfer news: New Alexis Mac Allister contract timeline given as two-year claim made (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 13:45

Liverpool are unlikely to give any consideration to a new contract for Alexis Mac Allister before February, Reds Champions League winner Didi Hamann has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The Argentina international is in the last two years of his current contract with Liverpool, having not signed a single extension since joining from Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2023.

Mac Allister revealed in September that Liverpool were not in a position to offer him a new contract, after the 27-year-old experienced a noticeable decline in individual performance levels in 2025-26.

However, after a positive World Cup with Argentina, Mac Allister has returned to form for Liverpool, scoring five goals and providing one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions so far this season.

The midfielder has started nine of Liverpool's 11 Premier League games under Andoni Iraola and also performed well in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United, creating two chances, completing 89% of his passes and winning four of his five ground duels.

Nevertheless, ex-Liverpool midfielder Hamann does not believe that talks over a new deal will begin for another three months, and any extension is only likely to be two years at best.

"They said to him there's no contract now, and he's in his late 20s," Hamann told Sports Mole when asked if Mac Allister had already played his way into a new contract.

"If he carries on performing, if he keeps on scoring goals, then come February, March, April, there might be a time where you say. 'maybe we keep him another two years.' But I don't think there's any rush at the moment."

Mac Allister - who turns 28 on December 24 - has come up with 24 goals and 21 assists in 167 matches for Liverpool since 2023, and he earns £180,000 a week under his current contract terms, according to Capology.

The Argentine's reported salary only makes him the 11th highest-paid player at Liverpool, below new signing Ronald Araujo (£210k) and almost half of what Virgil van Dijk earns (£350k).

Mac Allister's relationship with Ryan Gravenberch blossomed to the maximum in the 2024-25 season, culminating in both midfielders becoming Premier League champions for the first time.

However, Mac Allister's decline from a defensive and box-to-box standpoint was striking; compared to 2024-25, he made 45% fewer tackles and 26% fewer recoveries than in the 2025-26 campaign.

Gravenberch's own form did not help the South American's cause, though, and the latter has had a rejuvenated look about him since the World Cup, immediately earning Iraola's trust in the process.

Mac Allister's availability remains exceptional too, as he has only missed 11 matches for club and country since joining Liverpool and has been involved in every match so far this season.

With Wataru Endo almost certainly on the way out and James McConnell still on the fringes, Liverpool should speed up the process of tying down Mac Allister, lest they risk losing another midfield option in 2027.

Didi Hamann was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of Lottoland Live Casino.

There was a special moment for Jashari just after coming on at half-time as he scored the third goal of the night and his first for the club. It came in transition, with the Swiss midfielder running in behind and thumping a powerful shot in off the near post, leaving the goalkeeper stunned.

Jashari spoke to SportMediaset after the final whistle at San Siro to reflect on what was a great night both for the team and for him on a personal note, with his words via MilanPress.

“I hope so. I’m happy with today and I’ll try to continue like this for the team and the fans. It’s very important to have won.”

“In my opinion, it’s very important to continue like this. The season is too long until May. Now it’s November. We’ve had a good season so far, but there are five months to go until May. We need these results against all our opponents. Today it was Frosinone, there’s still a lot to do.

#1501. Man Utd make decision on what to do next after Leny Yoro's controversial red card against Liverpool

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 13:57, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 14:51

Manchester United have reportedly notified the FA of their intention to appeal Leny Yoro's red card.

The centre-back was sent off during Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday after bringing down Alexander Isak as the striker raced through on goal.

The Red Devils were reduced to 10 men just eight minutes into the contest, a moment that significantly altered the complexion of the game as Liverpool enjoyed greater possession and created better opportunities.

While Man Utd could arguably have done more to frustrate the Reds, there is little doubt that Yoro's dismissal had a major bearing on the outcome.

According to Sky Sports, the Red Devils intend to appeal Yoro's dismissal, with Mauricio Pochettino offering his interpretation of the incident after the game.

The main point of contention is whether the foul constituted a clear denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with questions surrounding whether Isak was actually in control of the ball.

Under the laws of the game, one of the considerations when determining whether a player should be sent off for Denying an Obvious Goal-Scoring Opportunity (DOGSO) is whether the attacking player had control of the ball.

Pochettino not only questioned that aspect of the decision but also highlighted the referee's failure to penalise Jeremy Jacquet for his challenge on Bryan Mbeumo at the opposite end just moments earlier.

It remains to be seen how the FA will assess the incidents, although former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher has backed the on-field decisions in both cases.

Unless the decision is overturned following an appeal, Yoro is set to serve a one-match domestic suspension rather than a three-match ban, as his denial of a obvious goalscoring opportunity was a non-violent offence.

While the defender is available to face Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, he will miss Man United's next Premier League fixture at home to Brentford on Saturday.

Yoro will then be available to return to Premier League action on December 2 when Pochettino's side travel to St James' Park to take on Newcastle United.

The Red Devils are now without a win in their last nine Premier League matches and have slipped to 19th in the table, with only Crystal Palace faring worse.

#1500. Drone operator apologises for filming Mauricio Pochettino's first training session, while Man United must apply to close airspace if they want to avoid another embarrassing security breach

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 04:54 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:58 EST, 20 November 2026

The drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session at Manchester United has removed the video from his YouTube account and apologised to the club.

United suffered the embarrassing security breach on Pochettino’s first day as head coach after the 12-minute footage showing the Argentine and his staff working with the players at Carrington was posted online.

The owner of the account called CC Overview, who is known only as Colin, justified the intrusion by saying that the airspace over Carrington is unrestricted and the drone was operating legally within Civil Aviation Authority rules.

United will have to apply to the Department of Transport if they want to close off the airspace to avoid more unwanted drones.

CC Overview took the video down on Friday morning insisting that he was unaware of the significance of his actions.

He also clarified that neither Liverpool – who are United’s opponents in Pochettino’s first game at Anfield on Sunday – nor any other club were involved in the filming.

Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session was filmed by a drone and the operator has now apologised

The drone user, who is known only as Colin, said he had not broken laws but apologised

United have declined to comment over the incident and it’s unclear if the club have made contact with him or involved Greater Manchester Police.

His statement read: ‘I would like to speak about yesterday’s incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.

‘My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time.

'I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

‘I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets.

'I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match. I would also like to state that Liverpool Football club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday.

‘The video has been removed from my channel. I have spent the past four years building up my YouTube channel and were well regarded in the fields I film and would now like to get back to building up my damaged reputation and making well received responsible videos. Thank you.’

United say they will not pursue legal action this time but will not hesitate to do so if it happens in the future.

To stop drones legally flying over Carrington, it has emerged that the club would need to seek permission from the Government to restrict the airspace around the training ground.

Footage of the session was captured close to Carrington and uploaded online

There are tight controls issued by the CAA and National Air Traffic Services over flying drones of different sizes, and a code of conduct related to how they are operated. It includes sharing photos and videos that could be ‘unfair’ to anyone.

It states that drones over 250g should not be flown closer than 50 metres to people, and drones below that weight should not be flown over crowds.

The drone and model aircraft code also states that you must ‘keep at least 150m away from residential, recreational, commercial and industrial areas’. It lists sports facilities as a recreational area.

Man United installed signs in 2018 warning that the use of drones over Carrington was 'strictly prohibited' and would be reported for prosecution

‘Think before sharing photos and videos. Avoid sharing anything that could be unfair or harmful to anyone. Think carefully about who could see your photos and videos – especially before posting them on social media. Apply the same common-sense approach that you would with images or video recorded on a smartphone or digital camera.’

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was asked about the drone on Friday, saying: 'It shouldn't be legal. There is a reason why we train behind closed doors. It's not nice for any club.'

#1499. Man City charges: Jeremy Doku's response to “juicy” discussion on guilty Premier League verdict

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 13:59

Jeremy Doku was the latest Manchester City player to be questioned on his thoughts regarding the club’s Premier League financial charges case during a press conference on Monday.

An independent commission has found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

In a verdict delivered at the end of September, the Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts with a number of commercial partners to disguise secret funding of more than £830m and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 campaigns.

Man City have repeatedly expressed their innocence and lodged an appeal last month, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”

Should Man City’s guilty verdict be upheld, the club would be in danger of a plethora of possible sanctions, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

On the pitch, Man City have recently suffered a dip in form, failing to win any of their last four Premier League games (D1 L3), but manager Enzo Maresca played down suggestions that the 115 charges case is distracting his players - something Didi Hamann disagrees with.

Since September’s verdict, the likes of captain Ruben Dias and star striker Erling Haaland have faced questions on the ongoing legal case, and Doku is now the latest City star to be asked for his views on the matter.

However, Doku politely declined to comment on the club’s situation and was keen to discuss on-field matters only when speaking to the media ahead of City’s Champions League clash with Napoli on Tuesday.

“I know this is all juicy for you guys, but we have a big week; Napoli tomorrow, and then Arsenal," the Belgium international told reporters on Monday.

"So I think there's enough to speak about there instead of speaking about the charges. I'm not the person to speak about the charges, so with all respect I don't really want to be on that topic. We can speak about football, that's no problem."

In August, just a month before the guilty verdict was published, Doku extended his contract with Man City until the summer of 2031, and the winger has no regrets over his decision.

"I signed because I was happy to sign. I didn't think about anything else,” Doku clearly stated after being asked whether the charges came into his conversations over a new contract.

"I don't think it was a difficult thing for me. When you look at this club, how big of a club it is, the trophies they won and everything, it was an easy choice for me.

"I was happy here, I am happy here, I have a wife here, a son, it was an easy choice for me. So I didn't think a lot, obviously everything needed to be right for me to sign, but as soon as everything was right on both sides, it was an easy choice for me."

Assessing Man City’s season so far from an individual and collective perspective, Doku added: "I think I can do better. I started off with an injury this season, then came back well.

“And then the team, we did well with the first seven [Premier League] games where we won, and afterwards it was a bit more tough. As everyone knows, at the moment it's a bit more difficult, but I'm sure we'll bounce back, me as well."

Doku is a strong contender to start for Man City in their Champions League clash against Napoli, with the Citizens seeking to move one step closer to automatic last-16 qualification having already won three of their first four League Phase matches.

Maresca, meanwhile, has provided a positive update on the fitness of right-back Matheus Nunes, who missed the 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham last weekend.

#1498. Rabiot and Ruben’s rampant Rossoneri: All the key stats from AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone

AC Milan produced their best attacking display of the season on Sunday night as they put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro.

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani early on set the tone, with Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netting in the rout. The ruthless counter-attacking display moves Milan back inside the top four, after wins from Como, Roma and Lazio earlier in the round.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The match stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals – so scoring double what they created – but also having five big chances which matches the number of goals scored.

Frosinone remarkably had more shots in total (15 to 12), but they were more wasteful with only three on target to the Rossoneri’s eight. The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season.

📊 The stats from the win against Frosinone. pic.twitter.com/ERVTj98m9Y

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 22, 2026

Only Nereo Rocco’s (29) and Lajos Czeizler’s (31) Milan sides scored more goals than Ruben Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 matches in charge in Serie A.

Adrien Rabiot is the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal (including goals and assists) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004, and he became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A with more than 10 goals in his first 10 games in a single season.

With his sixth goal in his 10th Serie A appearance for Milan at 20 years and 31 days, Alphadjo Cisse became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato , who achieved it at 18 years and 189 days.

No team has scored more goals than Milan in the first 15 minutes of play in the five major European leagues currently underway (7, like Barcelona and Chelsea).

Milan are now unbeaten in all seven meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W5 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

Milan have won five of their last six league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in a run of Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

Firstly, Fondazione Milan took centre stage at San Siro as Match Charity Partner of Milan-Frosinone, putting the stories of the people behind its projects at the heart of the pre-match.

#1491. Barcelona targeting January move for Tottenham Hotspur defender

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Tottenham could face growing interest in one of their key players ahead of the January transfer window, with Barcelona president Joan Laporta reportedly keen on bringing Pedro Porro to the Nou Camp.

The Spanish right-back has attracted attention following his performances for Spain at the World Cup, but Spurs have several reasons to feel confident about keeping hold of the defender.

According to Catalan broadcaster 3Cat, Porro is one of Laporta’s preferred defensive targets as Barcelona consider whether to strengthen their backline in January.

The Catalan club have been dealing with a series of defensive injuries involving Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart. However, Barcelona have not made a final decision on whether to bring in another defender, with the club waiting to assess the injured players’ recoveries.

Laporta’s admiration for Porro reportedly grew during Spain’s World Cup campaign. The Tottenham defender became an important part of the national team, developing a strong understanding with Lamine Yamal on the right flank and scoring twice during the tournament, including in the semi-final against France.

Laporta watched that semi-final in Dallas and was reportedly impressed by Porro’s performance. Barcelona had also gathered information about the defender towards the end of the previous summer transfer window, but their enquiry did not progress into a formal proposal to either the player or Tottenham.

Porro’s contractual situation gives Spurs a strong negotiating position. The 27-year-old renewed his contract shortly before the World Cup, committing his future to the north London club until 2031.

Reports have also indicated that Tottenham would demand a significant fee to consider allowing the defender to leave. Real Madrid have also been linked with an interest in the Spain international, potentially creating further competition for his signature.

Barcelona’s admiration for Porro is a reminder of the defender’s standing in European football, but there is currently no confirmed bid or formal approach.

Tottenham will be keen to retain a player who remains an important part of their plans. His long-term contract also means the club are under no immediate pressure to negotiate a sale.

The situation could develop if Barcelona decide their defensive injury problems require January reinforcements. For now, however, Spurs remain in a strong position, and any interested club would likely have to make a substantial offer to test their resolve.

#1490. Arsenal: Mikel Arteta issues David Raya injury update after worrying photo emerges

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 14:15

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya will miss Tuesday's Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund but appears to have avoided a serious injury, Mikel Arteta has announced.

The Spain international collided with Newcastle United striker Will Osula in the second half of Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw and had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya was in visible pain as an Arsenal physio supported his arm and shoulder, and Arteta admitted at full time that his number one having to come off was "not good news".

The Arsenal boss also revealed that Raya would undergo an MRI scan on Sunday to assess the seriousness of the issue, and on the same day, he was photographed with his arm in a sling in London.

@TouchlineX Raya yesterday in Oxford Circus... https://t.co/6NVmuNDLzZ

However, speaking to reporters in his pre-game press conference, Arteta delivered a reassuring update on Raya, who has seemingly avoided a fracture or dislocation and will not need to go under the knife.

"He’s not fit for tomorrow, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. It seems to be better than expected," Arteta told the media.

"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first test we have done shows something that is much more encouraging. There is no need for surgery. Tomorrow we will have more tests and we will know [more]."

Arteta did not directly rule Raya out of Sunday's Premier League clash with Manchester City either, potentially handing Arsenal a monumental boost ahead of the visit of Enzo Maresca's side.

The 31-year-old has already kept 10 clean sheets in 16 appearances for the Gunners this season, and he is also believed to have agreed a new long-term contract with Arsenal; his current deal expires in 2028.

Raya has only missed one Arsenal game through injury since originally joining on loan from Brentford in January 2023 - the 5-1 EFL Cup third-round win over Bolton Wanderers in September 2024.

With Raya sidelined, Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to make just his second Champions League start for Arsenal on Tuesday, after appearing in January's 3-2 victory over Kairat Almaty.

However, Arteta could throw a curveball and select Illan Meslier, whose first and only appearance for the Gunners so far came in their horrendous EFL Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.

The Frenchman has also never played in the Champions League in his career, while Kepa has appeared in the competition 22 times and was Chelsea's starting goalkeeper during their run to the 2022-23 quarter-finals.

As the latter has also held his position as Arteta's number two despite Meslier's arrival, there should be no doubt over Arsenal's starting goalkeeper against Borussia Dortmund.

#1489. Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions

Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o

The former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he said. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a new history here and I have started on the right foot.”

What an important week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

Régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

“Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães said. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”

These are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

And his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”

Raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh

Mikel Arteta launched a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

“In my opinion, that is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times,” said Arteta. “And I cannot find a way to understand how you think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

“I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

“You see, it is a judo roll and it brings the player on the floor. So how can this happen? I cannot find an explanation. That’s why I’m trying to find that.”

The win rounded off a positive week for Arsenal despite Arteta’s fury at the officials.

“I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place. We had really good periods but didn’t score and after that they can suffocate you especially when they decided to be really physical and very direct and we had to overcome a situation that in my opinion was absolutely unacceptable at this level. I’m very worried and very sad because this can never be a penalty ever.

“Are you surprised? Are you surprised? No. OK.

“Ezri does nothing. Just watch it. We have a lot of cameras and VAR, and we have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the game and the momentum which is a really, really serious thing,” he added.

“I’m making it very clear publicly because it’s for the game, it’s not only for Arsenal, this cannot happen at this level. We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that.”

Guimarães’s goal was his first for Arsenal, with Arteta adding: “Beautiful, he came on, the goal, the assist, remarkable. That why we talk about the finishers and making that impact and being able to support and help the team. He was outstanding.”

Three points or not, the Arsenal manager is furious about the penalty that was awarded to Sunderland.

I’m so upset – it’s unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This can change the course of a season, of the championship. I’ve seen it 10 times, to make sure, because I saw it live and said ‘It’s not possible at this level it can be a penalty’. Because it’s a judo roll, that’s what it is. It cannot happen.

I’ve been in football for 27 or 28 years - it’s not a penalty in any game, in any league, in any context.

Sunderland are a really, really good team and I don’t want to take any credit away from them. It’s been extremely tough and I’m really happy that we’ve done it.

"It's not a penalty in any case, in any game, in any context, in any league" 😳Mikel Arteta reflects on Arsenal's 2-0 win over Sunderland 👀@jules_breach | 📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/2BUZILexk3

I feel very good. It was a beautiful goal and a beautiful moment for me and my family.

It’s a very good place to score! Everyone knows my history at Newcastle; now I’m trying to create more history with Arsenal.

[Is David Raya the best goalkeeper in the world?] Definitely. This guy’s an unbelievable player.

What a goal! And especially the time he scored. Coming to this place is so difficult but we dealt with it very well.

It’s a big moment, especially at 0-0 away from home, and they were on top of us at the time.

Arsenal have won nine Premier League games in a row for the first since the Invincible season of 2003-04.

Three away games for Arsenal this season, three wins and three clean sheets. Nobody does it better. The Arsenal players will sleep well tonight because Sunderland made them work extremely hard for the three points.

The match was decided by a dramatic three-minute period early in the second half. Enzo Le Fee’s penalty was superbly saved by David Raya; then the Arsenal substitute – and former Newcastle captain – Bruno Guimares slammed a spectacular goal.

Bukayo Saka confirmed victory with an injury-time penalty. Arsenal are top of the table with 12 points out of 12; good luck trying to catch them.

90+7 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 2 (Saka pen) Bukayo Saka’s penalty goes through the hands of the diving Roefs and into the net. That should be the last kick of the game.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh

90+6 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 1 Saka is fouled by Reinildo, whose misery is compounded by a second yellow card.

Gabriel and Mukiele are booked for their part in that shoving match.

There’s a bit of pushing and shoving from players on both sides after a foul by Isidor on Guimaraes. Nothing much in it.

Sunderland have six minutes of added time in which to find an equaliser.

Arsenal substitution Mikel Merino for Martin Odegaard, presumably for his height at defensive set-pieces.

Big save from Raya! Xhaka takes a corner on the right, gets it back and curls another wicked ball into the six-yard box. Mukiele stretches to poke it towards goal and Raya paws the ball away. It loops up invitingly in front of goal - but then Raya is fouled by one of the Sunderland players charging desperately towards the ball.

A Sunderland corner loops up in the air and is volleyed acrobatically over the bar by Mukiele. That was a pretty good effort, and it only just cleared the bar.

Double change for Arsenal Eberechi Eze and Martin Zubimendi replace Christos Tzolis and... Declan Rice. He doesn’t look injured so it might just be workload management.

Brobbey pushes Gabriel over off the ball and is booked.

Disallowed goal Odegaard’s beautiful free-kick is headed in emphatically by Timber - but then the flag goes up for offside. Not much in it but the decision has been confirmed.

Sunderland substitution Malick Fofana replaces Thomas Meunier and creates a chance immediately with a thrilling run down the left. There’s an appeal for a penalty and then a close-range backheel from Mukiele that is blocked by Konsa.

Ballard clears off the line! Saka swings the resulting corner to the far post, where Havertz rises imperiously to head past Roefs. Ballard stoops towards his own goal and heads clear superbly. I’m not entirely sure Havertz’s header was on target but Ballard didn’t know that.

Moments later, Guimaraes curls just wide of the far post.

Fine save by Roefs! Arsenal cut Sunderland open on the break. Tzolis flicks a neat pass to Odegaard, who runs at a backpedalling defence and tees up Saka. His right-foot shot is beaten round the post by Roefs.

Eyebrows were raised at the £75m fee for Bruno Guimaraes, especially as he turns 29 in November, but Arsenal were willing to pay so much money because they knew the Brazilian was a sure thing. Only a player with serious experience of the Premier League could come into central midfield, off the bench, in a game like this and completely understand the tempo and flow of the game.

Sunderland substitution Wilson Isidor replaces Nilson Angulo.

Xhaka is booked for a sliding tackle on Guimaraes, though he got the ball and felt it was a clean challenge.

Chance for Arsenal Saka puts Havertz through on goal on the left side of the area. He eschews the shot and instead tries to find Tzolis with a square pass that is cut out by a Sunderland defender. Havertz may have been too selfless there.

Dan Ballard is booked - not sure whether it was a foul or for dissent.

The home fans have been stunned into relative silence by that double whammy. It was a mighty finish from Bruno Guimaraes.

58 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 1 (Guimaraes) A hammer blow from the former Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes! Sunderland looked set to go 1-0 up a moment ago; now they’re 1-0 down. Rice played a square pass to Guimaraes, lurking with intent just outside the D; he got the ball out of his feet and whipped an unstoppable curler into the top corner. What a way - and time, and place - to score your first Arsenal goal.

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88

54 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 0 A long throw from the left is claimed by David Raya - but the referee points to the spot after a wrestling manoeuvre by Konsa on Ballard!

Arsenal are furious, and that probably wouldn’t have been given last season, but clubs were told at the start of the season that wrestling would be penalised.

Gabriel goes down holding his jaw and claims he was elbowed by Ballard. VAR aren’t interested and the referee tells an irritated Gabriel to leave the field for one minute.

Konsa makes an important challenge on the relentless Brobbey, as does Gabriel on Le Fee a few seconds later. Sunderland keep pushing and Sadiki rakes a shot over the bar from the edge of the area.

Chance for Sunderland A long throw from the right isn’t cleared by Arsenal, and eventually Meunier hits a snapshot that is kicked away instinctively by David Raya. That’s a pretty good save.

Jurrien Timber and Bruno Guimaraes, who is popular in these parts, replace Ben White and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Tzolis’s deep cross is headed back into the six-yard box by Saka. Havertz stoops towards the ball but is beaten to it by Xhaka, a crucial bit of defending and the last action of a hard-fought, goalless first half.

Ben White has a groin problem and is going to be replaced by Jurrien Timber, either now or at half-time.

Xhaka’s dangerous corner is punched back to him by Raya. He picks out Le Fee, who drags a shot wide of the near post from 20 yards. Sunderland’s belief is growing.

Angulo goes down in the Arsenal area after a challenge from the side by White. Play continues and Meunier’s speuclative shot deflects behind for a corner.

Sunderland have been terrific in this first half.

Mikel Arteta is booked for encroaching outside his technical area. He responds by sticking his thumb up at the fourth official.

Mikel Arteta receives a yellow card for stepping out of the technical area 😅📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/xDlnL1B9MY

Arsenal are yet to score from a set piece this season. Their supporters have used that fact as evidence they are not as reliant on corners as their critics say, but the truth is that it will bother Arteta and set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. This is the sort of cagey game in which Arsenal so often made the breakthrough from a set piece last season.

Sunderland break through Mukiele, who charges into space and rifles a low drive that is blocked by Gabriel on the edge of the area.

The resulting corner leads to a brief VAR check for an Arsenal penalty after a bit of a wrestling match between Calafiori and Brobbey. Nothing given.

Good save by Roefs Saka curls a cross towards Havertz, who does well to control it on the chest while facing away from goal. He waits for the ball to bounce and hooks an imaginative shot that is fingertipped over by Roefs. Good save.

Chance for Arsenal Tzolis plays a nice pass down the side of the area for Odegaard. He cuts the ball back to Havertz, who screws a first-time shot over the bar. It was a slightly awkward chance because of the angle of Odegaard’s pass.

Reinildo is booked for a foul on Saka. The home fans are getting annoyed with what they perceive as diving from some of the Arsenal attackers: “Same old Arsenal, always cheating” is the chant of choice just now. Odegaard also went down a moment ago after a foul from Angulo.

Gabriel strides forward from defence and sweeps a left-foot shot from 25 yards. It’s a good effort that fades just wide of the far post with Roefs scrambling across his line.

Sunderland will be really pleased with the first quarter. They’re defending solidly and look a threat on the break, thanks in part to some outstanding hold-up play from Brian Brobbey. Saka’s volley is the only shot on target at either end.

Chance for Sunderland Brobbey does brilliantly to hold the ball and find Le Fee, who is fouled on the left wing by Gabriel. That allows Sunderland to send the centre-backs forward - and one of them, Dan Ballard, almost opens the scoring!

Xhaka curled a sensational ball around the Arsenal defence towards the far post, where the ball bounced up awkwardly and was knocked wide by either Ballard or Mukiele, who flew in at the far post. Ballard would have had an easier chance had Mukiele not got in the way.

Chance for Arsenal Saka mishits a volley straight at Roefs from close range after running onto a penetrative pass from Rice. It wasn’t an easy ball to take on the volley - Rice hit it very firmly - but Saka would usually do better.

The pattern of the game has been established, with Arsenal dominating the ball and Sunderland picking their moments to press and then counter-attack.

Looks like it will be a good battle between Brian Brobbey and Ezri Konsa. Brobbey seems to be attaching himself to Konsa, rather than getting into a scrap with Gabriel.

Sunderland break promisingly down the right. Mukiele drives an angled low cross that only just evades Angulo at the far post.

Calafiori has a shot from 18 yards blocked after a typical run infield from left-back.

Enzo Le Fee tries to score from inside his own half. David Raya was outside the penalty area but Le Fee completely mishit the shot.

Arsenal have started well and are dominating possession. So far it’s all been in front of the Sunderland defence, but you’d expect that to change if they continue to have this much of the ball.

The champions kick off from left to right as we watch.

There’s a pulsating atmosphere at the Stadium of Light - you’d expect nothing less - and the action is about to begin.

Myles Lewis Skelly is the first England teenager to start the first four league games of a season for Arsenal since Tony Adams and David Rocastle in the 1986/87 campaign.

We’re in a congested period right now. We’re playing midweek games as well. We made four changes against Napoli, we make another four for today and we try to keep all the players connected with a high level of confidence, and with the right chemistry in and around the team.

We know how tough Sunderland made it for every opponent here [last season] and we know the beautiful atmosphere that they create, the organisation that they have and the individuals that they have. We’ll try to impose ourselves like we always do and come here and be as dominant as we’ve been and then be ready to win the game.

Arsenal’s biggest rivals are still waiting for their first win - and their first goal - of the Premier League season. Alex Connor has reaction to their 0-0 draw at home to Everton.

"For sure we can improve, and we will" 😅Mikel Arteta on Arsenal's strong start to the season 🗣️📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nDpwooZq4Y

Arsenal keeper David Raya has conceded only one goal in five matches this season, but he was beaten twice on this ground last season during a thrilling 2-2 draw.

When will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the new £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

In the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

RLB's XI to take on Arsenal! ❤️👊#SUNARS pic.twitter.com/F1nXWky4Fp

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the Arsenal team that won in Napoli during the week. Kai Havertz’s return is the headline news in Arteta’s selection, with in-form left-back Riccardo Calafiori also returning. Myles Lewis-Skelly returns to the midfield and Christos Tzolis starts.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵 Your Saturday night Gunners ❤️‍🔥🤝 Presented by @deel

Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Leny Yoro, meanwhile, is available to return to the UCL squad after serving his own one-game ban following a red card against Atletico Madrid last month – he also received a straight red card in Man United’s heavy 4-0 Premier League defeat to Liverpool on Sunday, but will instead serve a domestic ban for that dismissal.

Matthijs de Ligt was handed his first PL start in 357 games by Pochettino after recovering from a long-term injury, but the Dutchman endured a difficult return to the Red Devils side and may be pulled out of the starting lineup in midweek.

Harry Maguire would be the most likely name to replace De Ligt and could start as one of three central defenders next to Yoro and Lisandro Martinez, with Diogo Dalot and Patrick Dorgu operating as wing-backs.

Kobbie Mainoo, Youri Tielemans and captain Bruno Fernandes are expected to continue in their central midfield roles, the latter is set to face his former club for the first time since leaving to join Man United in January 2020.

Bryan Mbeumo could retain his starting spot as a centre-forward, but Pochettino may be tempted to hand Joshua Zirkzee a rare start up front, with Mbeumo moving over to the right side of attack. However, Amad Diallo could instead play on the right which would likely keep Mbeumo through the middle.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:

Ruben Amorim had some interesting comments after the Frosinone win, including why he is not a fan of a term that is going viral.

Milan put on a five-star display at San Siro on Sunday night as they routed that Canarini. All five of their goals came via flowing counter-attacks, which has led to the tag ‘AmorimBall’ doing the rounds on social media, with many believing things are starting to truly click.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The head coach is keeping his feet firmly on the ground though, as he spoke after the game about the need to find consistency both within matches but also from game-to-game. In this sense, Thursday’s trip to face Olympiacos is another big test.

Amorim was present in the press conference room at San Siro following the win to answer questions from journalists, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“I don’t like that expression. I think we play games to win, we want to dominate the opponent. I don’t think we succeeded today: every game has its own story, and today it was man-on-man.

“Today we didn’t have to prepare much: the idea was simply to give the ball to Pulisic, to Moreira, and then exploit the combinations of these players, the understandings they already have, and conquer space.

“Today you saw that we didn’t spend much time near the opponent’s penalty area and we scored five goals, because the space wasn’t there, it was forty meters away to attack on the run.

“That’s why Cisse came on to play as a striker and not, for example, Camarda: because there was space behind him and Cisse is very good at that. So, I think we’ve played very good games in the past, but today it was just a question of the quality of the players, of one-on-ones, of reading the game.

“Today it wasn’t a question of the coach, I think, but of the players. And they, since it was man-on-man, just had to do what they can do. when they’re so good: beating the man and opening up space. So today the credit goes entirely to the players.”

“I watched the France game and I think he’s one of the best players on the team. So I think his importance is paramount. You can see there’s rotation, there’s a lot of talent. France has a lot of talent, but Rabiot is always there. There’s a reason for that.

“And then, if you look at the way France play, with Mbappé, with the way all these players position themselves on the pitch, sometimes with four players with Olise as the No. 10, he has to stay there to play a different kind of game.

“With us, he’s the player who has to push the team forward, he’s the decisive element. In France, however, he has a different job to do. So it depends more on his role in the national team and his role at Milan.

“This changes his way of interpreting the game, and it’s further proof of how Rabiot can play by adapting to the team he’s in. For me, therefore, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe. I hope his contract renewal comes soon.”

“Today’s match wasn’t just about tactics. We saw changes in position, one-on-one situations with plenty of space: it seemed like a crazy game. What I felt against Genoa and in the other matches was that we were too far away, we didn’t reach the final third of the pitch.

“We’re not like the big teams: if you look at the big teams, like Juventus, they might struggle to get results, but you see the volume they produce. For us, it’s a bit of the opposite, so I’m really worried that, if we don’t improve, we won’t be able to maintain this number of points.

“Today, however, was a step forward: we saw many players attacking the depth, something we hadn’t seen against Ferencvaros. In the other matches, we’d managed the ball well, but today we needed pace and runs.

“We need to be able to play both games within the same game, but today was clearly the type of game we needed to win.”

#1484. Big Decision From Manchester United Captain As Pochettino Is Set To Take Over

Manchester United transfer news: Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer, according to a report from The Athletic covered by CaughtOffside. The 32-year-old is unhappy with both the proposed salary and the length of the deal, and the standoff lands with his current contract set to expire in June 2027.

The calendar adds pressure. In 50 days, Fernandes can open talks with foreign clubs, and Galatasaray have already been linked. United hold a 12-month extension option that stops him leaving for free, but triggering it only postpones the argument and keeps an unhappy captain in the dressing room.

The refusal follows a bad few weeks. After a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics, and Carrick dropped him for the Bournemouth game. Carrick has since been sacked with United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, so Mauricio Pochettino inherits the standoff alongside a team in trouble.

His strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

Pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

United should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

The sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

If Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 15:29, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 15:34

Rangers play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday night looking to move to within one point of leaders Celtic in the Scottish Premiership table.

Meanwhile, Aberdeen make the trip to Ibrox knowing that they could move into the top six with a surprise win over the Glasgow giants.

Although missing out on European football came as a major blow to Rangers at the time, it has enabled Derek McInnes's side to build up a head of steam on the domestic front.

Rangers have put together a 13-match unbeaten streak since that exit to Jablonec in the Conference League playoff round, recording 11 wins and two draws.

While being held to a 2-2 draw at Hearts before the November international break frustrated McInnes, Rangers have responded with a victory over Aberdeen in the League Cup and successive top-flight triumphs.

A 2-0 success at St Mirren was followed by an hard-earned 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday, Rangers sealing the three points through an 88th-minute own goal.

Eight of Rangers' 13 league matches have been played away from Ibrox, giving them a chance to make the most of competing on home territory, with seven goals being scored in their last two such games in the Scottish Premiership.

Over the international break, Liechtenstein legend Mario Frick was named as the new Aberdeen head coach.

The surprise development was followed by Frick delivering a 4-2 victory at Kilmarnock in his first game in charge.

A much-needed win has led to the Dons moving into eighth spot, albeit still just three points above the relegation zone.

With Aberdeen having lost five of the six matches preceding his arrival, Frick will not be getting carried away with three points versus bottom-of-the-table opposition.

Nevertheless, Aberdeen have now accumulated seven points from their most recent four away games in the Scottish Premiership, something which cannot be ignored by their hosts.

If McInnes makes any changes to his Rangers XI, Findlay Curtis and Kevin Kelsy are favourites to be introduced in the final third.

While Cameron Devlin is making progress in his recovery from injury, this game is expected to come too soon for the midfielder. The same applies to Lawrence Shankland, who has recently returned to light training after a significant hamstring injury.

Ryan Naderi has contributed either a goal or assist in eight of his last nine Scottish Premiership appearances.

Afeez Aremu, Findlay Marshall and Ayoub Mouloua are all options to return for Aberdeen after they made an impact from the substitutes' bench at Kilmarnock.

Connor Ronan remains an injury doubt after missing that fixture, while this match comes too soon for defender Mats Knoester. Chris Cadden is pushing for a return to the squad after a hamstring issue.
